rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Cassino - Quick Rules 1.1 Overview 1.2 Gameplay 1.3 Scoring 1.4 Card Values Cassino - Quick Rules Overview Players: 2 to 4 (4 players usually play in partnerships). Deck: Standard 52-card deck (no Jokers). Objective: Capture cards from the table to score points. The game usually ends when a player/team reaches 21 points. Gameplay Each player is dealt 4 cards face down, and 4 cards are placed face up on the table. Play proceeds clockwise. On your turn, you must play exactly one card from your hand to perform one of the following: Pairing: Play a card that matches the rank of one or more cards on the table. You capture the played card and the matching table cards. Combining: Play a card that equals the sum of two or more cards on the table (e.g., play a 9 to capture a 5 and a 4). Building: Place a card from your hand onto a table card to create a combination for your next turn. You must hold the card required to capture the build (e.g., place a 3 on a 4 and announce "Building 7" if you have a 7 in hand). An opponent can "steal" a build by increasing its value (only for "single" builds). Trailing: If you cannot or do not want to capture or build, simply place one card face up on the table. Scoring Once all cards have been played, players score points based on their captured pile: Most Cards: 3 points (0 if tied). Most Spades: 1 point (0 if tied). 10 of Diamonds (Big Cassino): 2 points. 2 of Spades (Little Cassino): 1 point. Each Ace: 1 point (4 points total). Card Values Number Cards (2–10): Represent their face value. Aces: Count as 1. Face Cards (J, Q, K): Have no numerical value. They can only be captured by pairing (e.g., a King captures a King), not by combinations.

[Rating: 3/10] Like Koi-Koi, this will often see one player accomplish little but feeding their opponent. Unlike Koi-Koi, this has no novelty value for the Westerner.

[Rating: 3/10] Casino is a traditional card game about fishing, in which players use their cards in hands to gain cards from the table, directly, by matching the types or sum, or also by forming builds of cards, which players may take by playing a card which matches the total sum of the cards in the build. [Rating: 4/10] Fair.  I went through a phase where I loved to play this.  It's a nice little card game that has more opportunities for skill than appear at first glance.

[Rating: 4/10] Not a terrible standard card game. I've played it a lot and there are some tactics available, but the skills that make the most difference by far are card-counting and probability calculations. Far too much luck, however. Whoever gets dealt the 10 diamonds will win that card at least 80% of the time. In fact, avoiding playing cards that make 10s and or potential further builds to 10s is a tactic that should have a greater chance of success than it does. Overall, OK.

[Rating: 4/10] Played one 3-player game while waiting for a Tichu fourth. Like Cribbage in the sense that a better player can play a bit better, but you're really at the mercy of the cards. One play lef me with no urge for a second play.
